prompt: People living in the 21st century have a better quality of life than the previous centuries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some people argue that individuals alone should save for retirement and that governments should not be responsible for providing financial support in old age. I partly disagree with this view because personal responsibility is essential, but a complete withdrawal of state support would be unfair and socially damaging.

On the one hand, people should be encouraged to plan for their own retirement. Those who are physically and financially able to work during their adult lives have a duty to save, invest wisely and avoid unnecessary dependence on public funds. Personal savings, pension schemes and long-term financial planning can give retirees greater independence and reduce pressure on government budgets. For example, workers who contribute regularly to private or workplace pensions are less likely to experience hardship after leaving employment.

However, it is unrealistic to claim that governments have no obligation at all. Many people cannot accumulate sufficient savings because they work in low-paid jobs, suffer illness, care for family members or experience unemployment. If the state refuses to support such citizens, old age may become a period of poverty and insecurity. A basic public pension is therefore not merely a financial benefit but a form of social protection. Since people pay taxes throughout their working lives, it is reasonable for them to expect some support when they are no longer able to earn.

The most sensible approach is a shared system. Individuals should save according to their means, while governments should guarantee a minimum standard of living for the elderly. This would reward personal responsibility without abandoning vulnerable citizens.

In conclusion, retirement should not be viewed as the sole responsibility of either individuals or the state. A fair society requires citizens to prepare for the future, but it also requires governments to protect older people from poverty and neglect.
